definitions.gloss: to complain; to grumble; to find fault
definitions.explanation: To express dissatisfaction or objection about something, often repeatedly or in a nagging manner.

examples.japanese: {文句|もんく}ばかり{言|い}うな。
{料理|りょうり}に{文句|もんく}を{言|い}われて{傷|きず}ついた。
examples.english: I was hurt when someone complained about my cooking.

examples.japanese: {何|なに}をやっても{文句|もんく}を{言|い}う{人|ひと}がいるから、{気|き}にしないほうがいい。
examples.english: There are people who complain no matter what you do, so it's better not to worry about it.

notes:
One of the most common expressions for complaining in Japanese. {文句|もんく} by itself can mean "complaint" or "objection," and {文句|もんく}を{言|い}う is the standard verb phrase.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {文句|もんく}ばかり{言|い}う: to do nothing but complain
- {文句|もんく}を{言|い}われる: to be complained at (passive)
- {文句|もんく}があるなら{言|い}え: if you have a complaint, say it
- {文句|もんく}なし: no complaints; perfect

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {愚痴|ぐち}を{言|い}う/{愚痴|ぐち}をこぼす: to grumble, to vent — more about venting without expecting change
- {不満|ふまん}を{言|い}う: to express dissatisfaction — more formal
- {苦情|くじょう}を{言|い}う: to make a formal complaint — stronger, more official
- ぶつぶつ{言|い}う: to mutter complaints — emphasizes the manner (muttering)

USAGE:
{文句|もんく}を{言|い}う often has a slightly negative connotation, suggesting the complaints are excessive or unreasonable. {苦情|くじょう} is more neutral and implies a legitimate grievance.
